comments.body:
This (shape=[2, 2]) works
```python
x = torch.tensor([[1., 2.], [3., 4.]]).cuda()
```
This (shape=[2, 2, 1]) works:
```python
x = torch.tensor([[[1.], [2.]], [[3.], [4.]]]).cuda()
```
This (shape=[1, 2, 2]) doesn't work:
```python
x = torch.tensor([[[1., 2.], [3., 4.]]]).cuda()
```

So I think it's just leading singleton dim

Actually, these also don't work:
(shape=[2,1,1])
```python
x = torch.tensor([[[1.]],[[1.]]]).cuda()
```
(shape=[2,1,2])
```python
x = torch.tensor([[[1.,1.]],[[1.,1.]]]).cuda()
```

actually this fixes the error: ```python def t2j(x_torch): shape = x_torch.shape x_torch_flat = torch.flatten(x_torch) x_jax = jax_dlpack.from_dlpack(torch_dlpack.to_dlpack(x_torch_flat)) return x_jax.reshape(shape) ``` but then backprop doesn't work...
Context: [tweet](https://twitter.com/SingularMattrix/status/1623919590547009536) @hawkinsp might this be an easy fix?
Note you'll need to build jaxlib from source at head with an up to date XLA (TF) pin. Or you can wait until the next jaxlib release, which probably won't be that far off.
@sokrypton if there are other problems with jax2torch + AlphaFold, let us know! It seems like a good end-to-end test case.

issue.body:
[XLA:Python] Fix overly pessimistic handling of singleton dimensions in dlpack code.

Requires an accompanying jaxlib change.

Fixes https://github.com/google/jax/issues/14399
